summary.headline: Amber Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 13% to INR3,888 crore and operating EBITDA 28% to INR337 crore, with Electronics EBITDA more than doubling.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 13% YoY to INR3,888 crore and operating EBITDA grew 28% to INR337 crore, with adjusted PAT of INR126 crore (up 19%) before a INR123 crore exceptional loss. Electronics was the standout, with revenue up 29% and EBITDA more than doubling to a 10.8% margin. Railway & Defense EBITDA fell 26% on mix, copper, currency and Haryana minimum wage hikes. Management flagged that PCB margins were compressed by a roughly two-quarter pass-through lag and that cost pressure persists through H1, while Q1 benefited from pre-stocking of compressors and copper. The IL JIN facility incident was a new overhang, with insurance cover and the impact still being assessed.

segments.name: Consumer Durable
segments.commentary: Revenue INR2,758 crore (+8%) and EBITDA INR214 crore (+12%) despite commodity and minimum wage headwinds; management attributed the modest growth to a high base. RAC is roughly 55-60% of the division, with the remainder non-RAC.

segments.name: Electronics
segments.commentary: Revenue INR985 crore (+29%) and EBITDA INR107 crore (10.8% margin, up from about 6.4%). Bare PCB margin compressed on copper clad laminate (CCL) costs, and the EMS segment grew more slowly as customers destocked and shifted to job work. Management reiterated FY27 growth of about 40%.

segments.name: Railway Sub-systems & Defense
segments.commentary: Revenue INR144 crore (+18%) but EBITDA fell 26% to INR16 crore on product mix, including first trains supplied through a principal, plus copper, currency and a 35% Haryana minimum wage hike. FY27 revenue growth guided at 30-35% and EBITDA margin at 15-16%.

guidance_outlook: Electronics: FY27 growth of about 40% reiterated; EMS full-year guidance intact per Sanjay Arora.
Railway Sub-systems & Defense: FY27 revenue growth 30-35% and EBITDA margin 15-16%.
Consumer Durable: growth in line with RAC industry, cited as 13-15%; no percentage margin guidance given.
Group margin: earlier 50-100 bps decline guidance for FY27 now moderated, with margins seen normalising if no further currency or commodity disruption.
PCB margin: currently about 12% versus about 16% normal; expected to recover from Q3 FY27 to a 15-16% normalised range, subject to no further CCL price rises.

Oppo mobile: trial production in Q4 FY27, commercial production from Q1 FY28, about 8 million units in year one, rising to 15-16 million in year two; revenue-recognition model to be clarified in 15-20 days.
IL JIN: fundraise enabling resolution up to INR5,000 crore; quantum and form not yet decided. IL JIN production impact being assessed, with guidance expected to be met.
capex_capacity: PCB capex: about INR3,200 crore at Jewar (UP), where construction has started and trial production is about 18 months away; Hosur (Tamil Nadu) about INR1,000 crore, with the plant to be running this financial year; Shogini (Pune) INR500 crore. All three were approved under the ECMS scheme.
Jewar HDI PCB groundbreaking held with Ascent-K / Korea Circuit; air conditioner plant construction planned to start in 2028, with trial production in 2029.
Sidwal greenfield facility in Faridabad (HVAC, pantry, doors, gangways) is now operational.
Asset turn in PCB business about 0.8:1 depending on complexity.
CCL backward integration: Amber in discussion with JV partners; target own CCL plants by 2029-30.
demand_pricing: Consumer Durable: BEE tonnage labelling mandatory from 1 July 2026 has created mixed inventory in the trade; management expects inventory to clear by Diwali, a strong summer from November, and not very high festive demand.
Q1 Consumer Durable margins were helped by pre-buying of compressors and copper ahead of QCO enforcement, and by a premium mix (5-star and 2-tonne). Management said this would not be annualised.
PCB: pass-through to customers is progressing, with some customers raising prices in July. Copper clad laminate prices keep rising, driven by AI and data-centre demand and a shortage.
Electronics TAM: management cited $185 billion of electronics consumption, a $16-17 billion addressable market for PCB, PCBA and power electronics today, and an estimated $35-40 billion by FY30.
Power electronics (PLC, HMI, solar inverters, UPS, BESS) expected to grow 35-40%.

financial_highlights.change: +19% YoY (vs INR106 crore); INR141 crore before INR15.35 crore purchase-price-allocation inventory impact
vs around INR510 crore at March 2026

qa_highlights.question: Santhosh Seshadri (Avendus) asked about Oppo mobile export discussions, PLI eligibility, and PCB fixed-price contract exposure.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said export talks with Oppo are early and export would be considered after one year of domestic production; three ECMS approvals (INR3,200 crore Jewar, about INR1,000 crore Hosur, INR500 crore Shogini) are in place; PCB pass-through runs on a two-quarter lag as tier-2 supplier, with some customers already raising prices in July. Draft PLI guidelines are awaited.

qa_highlights.question: Aditya Bhartia (Investec) asked whether Q1 consumer durable margins reflected raw material inflation and inventory benefit, and about H1 margin outlook.
qa_highlights.answer: Sachin Gupta said Q1 benefited from pre-stocking of compressors and copper ahead of QCO enforcement and a premium mix (5-star and 2-tonne), which will not be annualised. He said margins are not expected to compress and the full-year outlook remains in line with projections.

qa_highlights.question: Aditya Bhartia asked about the operational impact of the IL JIN incident.
qa_highlights.answer: Jasbir Singh said reconstruction permission was received the previous day and assessment is under way. Guided numbers for the quarter are still expected to be met, and exchanges will be informed.

qa_highlights.question: Dhruv Jain (Ambit) asked why Electronics growth looks lower excluding acquisitions, and about FY27 guidance and railway margin outlook.
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Arora said EMS growth slowed because customers destocked and some shifted to job work, and smart meter and smart watch segments declined; full-year EMS guidance is intact. For Railways, Jasbir Singh guided FY27 revenue growth of 30-35% and margin of 15-16%, citing fixed-price railway contracts and first trains supplied through a principal.

qa_highlights.question: Keshav Lahoti (HDFC Securities) asked why minority interest swung from INR28 crore positive to INR19 crore negative, and about the IL JIN incident impact.
qa_highlights.answer: Sudhir Goyal said the swing was checked later: the INR123 crore exceptional loss sits in Electronics entities with minority holders, pushing the minority share negative. Jasbir Singh said assets are insured, production has shifted to other IL JIN locations, and the impact will be quantified within a week.

qa_highlights.question: Sameet Sinha (Macquarie) asked about input cost pass-through timing and local CCL manufacturing.
qa_highlights.answer: Jasbir Singh said consumer durable is tier 1 with a one-quarter lag, while PCB is tier 2 with a two-quarter lag, so pass-through starts from Q4. A first Wipro CCL plant is nearly operational, two more are planned, and Amber is in JV talks targeting own CCL plants by FY29-30.

qa_highlights.question: Achal Lohade (Nuvama) asked about PCB margin quantum, next-two-quarter margin path, and drivers of the 40% Electronics growth.
qa_highlights.answer: Jasbir Singh said normalised PCB margin is about 16% versus about 12% now, with Q2 still impacted and recovery from Q3 to a 15-16% range, subject to no further CCL price rises. All three Electronics divisions (PCBA, PCB, industrial power electronics) are expected to drive the 40% growth. Sudhir Goyal said a group-level minority percentage cannot be given.

qa_highlights.question: Bhavik Mehta (JP Morgan) asked whether the consumer durable industry growth and the 50-100 bps FY27 margin decline guidance still hold, and the timing of Oppo revenue recognition clarity.
qa_highlights.answer: Sachin Gupta said consumer durable growth is in line with industry, cited at 13-15%. Jasbir Singh said the 50-100 bps decline is moderated, with margins normalising absent further currency or commodity disruption. Oppo revenue-recognition clarity is expected in 15-20 days.

qa_highlights.question: Indrajit Agarwal (CLSA) asked about Oppo revenue booking entity, minority stake in IL JIN, and consolidated net debt.
qa_highlights.answer: Jasbir Singh said the booking entity (IL JIN or Amber) depends on ERP integration and will be formalised before mid-September. Sudhir Goyal said minority is computed on a diluted basis of about 60% with about 39-40% treated as minority interest, and net debt was about INR1,225 crore at 30 June 2026 versus about INR510 crore at March 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Rahul Agarwal (IKIGAI) asked for an entity-wise Electronics revenue build-up over three years.
qa_highlights.answer: Jasbir Singh declined a three-year number, citing asset turn of 0.8:1 and the capex plan (Jewar INR3,200 crore, Hosur INR1,000 crore). Power electronics is guided to grow 35-40%, and the Electronics TAM is $16-17 billion today, estimated at $35-40 billion by FY30. He did not accept the INR5,000 crore consolidated electronics sales framing.

risks_watch: IL JIN facility incident: final loss quantification and insurance recovery still pending; management promised an update within a week and a reassessment of the guided numbers.
PCB margin recovery depends on customer price pass-through and no further CCL price increases; Q2 FY27 is expected to remain impacted at about 12% margin versus about 16% normal.
Q1 consumer durable margin benefited from pre-stocking and a premium mix that management said will not be annualised; watch for normalisation as the BEE tonnage labelling mix clears by Diwali.

Net debt rose to about INR1,225 crore at 30 June 2026 from about INR510 crore at March 2026, alongside a fundraise enabling resolution of up to INR5,000 crore at IL JIN with quantum and form undecided.
Oppo mobile: revenue-recognition model (IL JIN vs Amber level) to be decided by mid-September; PLI eligibility depends on draft guidelines not yet issued; trial production targeted for Q4 FY27.
Minority interest swung to negative INR19 crore from positive INR28 crore; the adjusted minority figure was not provided on the call and was to be calculated later.
key_quotes: But what we have seen in July is that there are some customers who have increased the cost. So our margins are coming back to where it was.
But let me tell everybody on the call that the guided number of what we did last quarter, we are hopeful that we should be in line to deliver despite of this disruption.
So we are not looking at any margin compression.
But only subject to no further CCL price increases are happening.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth, the Oppo project, and the 40% Electronics and 30-35% Railways guidance, but cautious and evasive on near-term margins, the IL JIN impact, and any quantified multi-year targets. Management repeatedly declined to give numbers on consumer durable margins, three-year revenue build-up, and group minority allocation, citing volatility.
